title: Confidence-threshold routing to a human review desk
scenario: Model predictions are auto-accepted or sent to humans by per-(model, label) thresholds, the human queue is assigned to language-matched reviewers by priority (1 = most urgent) and capacity, and a calibration report plus JSON export round it off.

verified.why_correct: Dividing only when the number is above 1 looks like it mishandles values such as `1%`, but the README defines any value above 1 as a percentage, so `1` is 1.0 and `91`/`91%` are 0.91. Blank values return None as the spec requires.

The `>=` looks like it should be `>`, but the spec says that on equal timestamps the later row wins. It compares parsed datetimes, so the mixed formats order correctly, and the id is normalised before the lookup so ` P-05`/`p-02` collapse onto their twins.

bugs.title: Threshold cache keyed by label only
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_1_thresholds_for_v2_items: v2 items report v1 thresholds (P-03/P-04/P-11 show 0.8 instead of 0.95, P-06 0.9 instead of 0.92, P-08 0.85 instead of 0.88). Every decision is still the same.
bugs.why: The memo key drops the model version, so whichever model asks for a label first fixes the threshold for every model. v2 spam items get v1's 0.80 instead of 0.95; the data keeps every decision the same, so only the reported threshold reveals it.
hints: Compare the threshold reported for P-03 with the v2 spam row in thresholds.csv.
The table resolves correctly; look at what is remembered between lookups.
ThresholdTable.lookup caches by `label`; the key must be `(model_version, label)`.
probes: Why did every decision stay the same even though the thresholds changed?
What input order would have made this cache return the v2 value for v1 items instead?

bugs.title: Confidence equal to threshold sent to humans
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_2_decisions: P-07 is routed to 'human' instead of 'auto'. Nothing else changes, because P-07 is Portuguese and no reviewer speaks it.
bugs.why: The spec auto-accepts at exactly the threshold. With `>` P-07 (0.75 against the v1 ads threshold 0.75) is routed to a human.
hints: Which single item changed decision? Compare its confidence to its threshold.
Check the comparison in route_one against README rule 3.
probes: Why didn't the extra human item change any reviewer's assignments?
Floats: could 75% and 0.75 ever compare unequal here? Why not?

bugs.title: Queue sorted least urgent first
bugs.old: return sorted(pending, key=lambda p: (p.priority, p.received_at, p.item_id))
bugs.new: return sorted(pending, key=lambda p: (-p.priority, p.received_at, p.item_id))
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_3_english_reviewers: r-01 gets ['P-14', 'P-04'] and r-06 gets ['P-15', 'P-02'] instead of ['P-02', 'P-04'] and ['P-11', 'P-14']. The priority-1 item P-11 ends up unassigned.
bugs.why: Priority 1 is the most urgent, so it must sort ascending. Negating it hands out priority-3 items first; English capacity runs out and a priority-1 item is left unassigned.
hints: English has 6 human items and 5 slots. Which one should be left over?
Look at how the queue is ordered before assignment.
review_queue sorts by `-p.priority`; README rule 4 says 1 is most urgent, so sort by `p.priority`.
probes: Why were the German assignments unaffected by the queue order?
The comment says 'most urgent first'. What in the data tells you which end is urgent?

        capacity = DEFAULT_CAPACITY if capacity in (None, "") else int(capacity)
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_4_german_reviewers: r-07 receives ['P-17'] (expected []), and r-05 takes P-18 instead of P-17.
bugs.why: `0 or DEFAULT_CAPACITY` is 2, so r-07, who is off rotation, receives German items. Only a missing or blank capacity should get the default.

`int(item.get('capacity') or DEFAULT_CAPACITY)` turns 0 into 2; only apply the default for None or blank.

bugs.title: Counter.update fed a string
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_5_reviewer_mix: the per-reviewer counts are keyed by single letters, e.g. r-01 → {'a': 3, 'h': 1, 'm': 3, 'p': 2, 's': 2} instead of {'ham': 1, 'spam': 2}.
bugs.why: Counter.update iterates its argument, so a bare string counts its characters (`s`, `p`, `a`, `m`) rather than the label.
hints: What are the keys in reviewer_mix? Do they look like labels?
Look at how each reviewer's Counter is updated.
probes: Why did `agreement` come out right while reviewer_mix did not?

bugs.title: Datetimes exported with str()
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_6_exported_timestamps: exported last_review_at is '2026-03-01 16:45:00' instead of '2026-03-01T16:45:00' (space instead of T).
bugs.why: `default=str` serialises datetimes as `2026-03-02 11:05:00` (space separator) instead of ISO 8601, and would also write sets as `{...}` strings. The `_encode` helper does what the README asks.
hints: Compare the exported timestamp string character by character with the expected one.
How does export_json turn non-JSON types into strings?
probes: Why didn't json.dumps raise on the datetime values?
What would `default=str` do to a set of languages if one were added to the report?

context_qa.q: What happens inside build_report(), in order?
context_qa.a: It builds a ThresholdTable from thresholds.csv, loads and de-duplicates predictions, loads reviewers, routes every prediction (`route_all`), builds the human queue (`review_queue`), assigns it (`assign`, which appends into each Reviewer's `assigned` list and returns the unassigned ids), computes SLA due times for the queue, and runs `calibrate` over reviews.csv.

context_qa.q: How does ThresholdTable find a threshold?
context_qa.a: `_resolve` checks the exact `(model_version, label)` row, then the model's `*` row, then falls back to DEFAULT_THRESHOLD (0.90). `lookup` wraps `_resolve` with a dict cache stored on the instance, so each key is resolved once per table.
`capacity - len(assigned)`, computed live from the reviewer's `assigned` list, so it shrinks as `assign` hands out items.
It filters to active reviewers who speak the item's language and have `remaining > 0`, then takes `min` by `(-remaining, id)`: most remaining capacity first, then lowest id.
Only rows whose cleaned `human_label` is non-empty. Those feed `agreement_rates`, `reviewer_mix` and the max of `finished_at`.

context_qa.q: How does the loader read capacity and active?
context_qa.a: `load_reviewers` reads `capacity` from each JSON entry and converts it to int, using DEFAULT_CAPACITY (2) when it has no usable value. `active` is True only when the JSON value is literally `true`, defaulting to True when the key is missing.

context_qa.q: What is in the sla section and what type are its values?
context_qa.a: One entry per item in the review queue (human decisions only), mapping item id to `received_at + SLA_HOURS[priority]` as a `datetime`. `export_json` is what turns those into strings.
